answer_raw:
**Renting is the better financial move** if you are planning to move within one to two years.

A short holding period is very expensive per year of use; if you buy and sell within three years, you will likely be behind where renting would have left you unless the market moves sharply in your favor [7]. Buying is generally better only if you are confident you will stay put for at least **five to seven years** [7].

Because you are looking at a one-to-two-year window, the transaction costs of buying and the potential for being locked into a property you need to sell quickly make renting the more logical choice. If you were moving to a market like Mumbai, where the price-to-rent ratio is between 35 and 48 times annual rent (as of August 2026), the capital tied up in a purchase would be substantial [5].

Once you reach Latin America, you will have access to different investment profiles. For example, Medellín currently offers a high gross rental yield of around **9.17%** (as of October 2026) [1]. Buenos Aires also serves as a top Airbnb market with roughly **73% occupancy** (as of October 2026) [1].

Since I do not know your current city or local market conditions, you should check your local property tax, closing costs, and current mortgage rates to confirm the exact cost of a "short-term" ownership vs. renting.
